content: Could you describe the core messaging and buddy-list capabilities the application must support, including any specific rules for presence updates, nickname management, blocking contacts, and message notifications?

The application needs to let a user send and receive plain text instant messages with people on their buddy list, and it should show which buddies are currently online and, when available, what program or channel they’re watching. Users should be able to add and remove buddies, see their presence status update in near real time, and change their own nickname so it’s reflected to others. If a contact is blocked, that person should no longer be able to message the user or appear as available in the normal buddy view, and incoming messages should trigger a clear visible on-screen notification so the user knows something has arrived even if they’re not actively in the chat.

When a recipient is offline or unavailable, should the system queue incoming messages for later delivery and keep message history available for viewing, and if so, how long should those messages and chat logs be retained?

Yes, I’d expect offline messages to be queued so they can be delivered when the recipient comes back online, as long as that fits the platform’s messaging model. I’m not sure we’ve decided the retention period yet for queued messages or chat history, so I’d need to check with the team on how long we want to keep them and whether users should be able to view older logs from the TV interface.

What retention and access rules should apply to message data: how long should queued offline messages and chat history be kept, when should queued messages expire if a recipient does not return online, and should users be able to view past chat history from the TV interface?

I don’t have a firm policy for the exact retention period yet, so that would need to be confirmed with the team. My expectation is that queued offline messages should not be kept indefinitely; they should expire after some reasonable window if the recipient never comes back online, and chat history should be limited rather than permanent for privacy and storage reasons. For the TV interface, I’d want at least recent conversation history available to view, but I can’t say yet whether we should support full past logs or only the current session until that’s decided.

What privacy controls should users have over their presence visibility and sharing of viewing activity—for example, should they be able to appear offline, hide what program or channel they’re watching, or limit that information to certain buddies or groups?

Yes, users should have some control over that. At minimum they should be able to appear offline if they want to, and they should be able to hide what they’re watching from other users. I’m not sure yet whether we want finer-grained controls like sharing that activity only with certain buddies or groups, so that would need to be verified.
